decision_lens: For D7 (Inglehart class-interaction shape), which functional form — multiplicative-on-cohort, additive-baseline-diff, or class-stratified-independent — is most consistent with Inglehart (1997)'s reported cross-tabulations of post-materialist index by class and cohort? And for D2-Family2, does the proposed 63-cell table reflect that finding, or does it over-encode a multiplicative interaction the data does not support?
focus: Inglehart-Welzel post-materialist transition scholarship for Deliverables 2-Family2, 2-Family5, and 7: whether the Inglehart materialist/post-materialist class-by-posture multiplier table (D2-F2) correctly encodes the Inglehart 1997 finding as additive-baseline-diff (D7), whether class-stratified extrapolations respect the boundaries of the World Values Survey data, and whether the vocation-substrate couplings (D2-F5) are consistent with Inglehart's sectoral post-materialist findings.
name: fd-inglehart-postmaterialist-class-shape
persona: Apply the perspective of a comparative political culture researcher grounded in Inglehart's Values Surveys tradition (Inglehart 1977, 1997; Inglehart-Welzel 2005) and the class-stratified post-materialism literature — they care about whether the proposed class × posture multiplier table correctly represents Inglehart's finding that post-materialism rises with class AND cohort as an additive shift (not a multiplicative interaction), measure success by whether the 63-cell D2-Family2 table can distinguish which cells are directly supported by WVS cross-tabulations vs. which require extrapolation beyond the survey's class categories, and flag any proposed multiplier that treats class and cohort as multiplicatively interacting when Inglehart's own analysis supports only additive shifts.
review_areas: Inglehart additive-vs-multiplicative evidence: Inglehart (1997) reports post-materialist index scores by occupational class (working class, middle class, upper-middle class) and by birth cohort in tables that show class raising the baseline proportion of post-materialists at every cohort level. This is an additive pattern: the class-gap is roughly constant across cohorts, not widening or narrowing with cohort. A multiplicative-on-cohort model predicts that class differences are amplified at later cohorts (the class gap grows); the data does not clearly support this. Assess whether the D7 proposal correctly identifies additive-baseline-diff as the Inglehart-consistent form, and whether D2-Family2's proposed multipliers reflect additive shifts (small, consistent adjustments per class tier) rather than large multiplicative amplifications for high-class × late-cohort combinations.

WVS class-vocabulary mapping: Inglehart's WVS class categories (working class, lower-middle, middle class, upper-middle, upper) do not map cleanly onto the 9 Unc Rancher class values (working-class, service-precariat, blue-collar-skilled, lower-middle, professional, technical-knowledge, tech-money, old-money, scapegrace). The 9-value vocabulary includes technology-specific classes (tech-money, technical-knowledge) that postdate Inglehart's main data collection period and the scapegrace category that has no WVS analog. Assess which of the 9 class values can be reasonably mapped to WVS categories and which require estimate-tier treatment, and flag any proposed D2-Family2 multiplier for tech-money or scapegrace that is cited as literature-tier when no WVS data covers those categories.

Post-materialist shift and vocationally-absorbed posture coupling: Inglehart's finding is that post-materialist orientation is more common among professional and knowledge-sector workers — a finding the vocationally-absorbed posture is designed to capture. D2-Family2 should show professional, technical-knowledge, and tech-money classes lifting the vocationally-absorbed posture probability. Assess whether the proposed multipliers for these cells are consistent with Inglehart's reported class gap in post-materialism (which is substantial — upper-middle class post-materialists may be 2–3× more common than working-class post-materialists in WVS data) and whether a max_multiplier: 4.5 cap creates any compression problem for the Inglehart-warranted magnitude.

D2-Family5 vocation-substrate couplings vs. Inglehart sectoral analysis: D2-Family5 specifies 4 couplings (enforcement-order→vocational, survivor-vocation→single-anchor, clinical-care→vocational, land-work→vocational). Inglehart's sectoral analysis in post-industrial society research provides some grounding for public-sector occupational identities (enforcement, clinical-care) being more institution-aligned. Assess whether the proposed multiplier magnitudes for these couplings are consistent with sectoral post-materialism findings, or whether they are primarily grounded in synthesis-2026-05-20 (which is not an external empirical source) and should be marked estimate.

Cohort × class interaction bound check: the D2-Family2 63-cell table is class × posture, but the Inglehart finding fundamentally involves a three-way interaction (class × cohort × post-materialism). If the matrix separates the cohort effect into Ghitza-Gelman Family1 and the class effect into Inglehart Family2, the two families will compose multiplicatively at runtime. Assess whether the multiplicative composition of Family1 (era-to-posture imprinting) and Family2 (class-to-posture Inglehart shift) produces an implied joint distribution that is consistent with the Inglehart finding — or whether the two-family separation over-encodes the interaction effect by double-counting the class-by-cohort relationship.

Extrapolation bounds for contemporary cohorts: Inglehart's primary data ends in the mid-1990s. The Unc Rancher axis includes post-2020 era and social-platform and fragmented-feed media eras, which are well outside the WVS data's temporal scope. Assess which D2-Family2 cells for chronological_era=2010s or post-2020 Uncs can legitimately cite Inglehart-1997 vs. which require estimate-tier treatment with a rationale acknowledging the temporal extrapolation.

severity_examples.condition: If the synthesis proposes a multiplier of 3.0 for tech-money × vocationally-absorbed citing inglehart-1997 and interpreting the class-cohort interaction as multiplicative, but Inglehart's actual table for upper-middle class vs. working class post-materialism shows a ~2× absolute prevalence difference (not a 3× multiplicative amplification), the proposed value over-encodes the finding. A 3.0 multiplier cannot be justified from the inglehart-1997 source alone; the excess above the data-supported ~2× must be marked estimate.
severity_examples.scenario: D2-Family2 proposes multiplicative-on-cohort for tech-money × vocationally-absorbed, amplifying the posture 3× when the Inglehart data supports only an additive ~1.5× shift for the closest WVS analog

severity_examples.condition: If the synthesis assigns inglehart-1997 as source_tier for multipliers on tech-money or scapegrace cells, any reviewer who checks the WVS class categories will find no matching category. Tech-money (new-economy wealth) and scapegrace (social-margin dropout class) are post-1997 constructs with no WVS survey instrument. These cells must be source_tier: estimate regardless of what class-adjacent Inglehart findings might be invoked by analogy.
severity_examples.scenario: tech-money and scapegrace class cells in D2-Family2 are cited as inglehart-1997 literature-tier when no WVS category maps to these classes

severity_examples.condition: If Family1 (Ghitza-Gelman) gives a multiplier for 2010s era lifting vocationally-absorbed, and Family2 (Inglehart) gives a separate multiplier for professional class lifting vocationally-absorbed, and these compose multiplicatively at runtime, the joint effect for professional × 2010s may be 2.5 × 1.8 = 4.5 — hitting the max_multiplier cap — even though the empirical joint probability of vocationally-absorbed for professional 2010s Uncs may only be ~1.5× the baseline. Flag if the two families need attenuation to avoid compounding the interaction.
severity_examples.scenario: D2-Family1 and D2-Family2 together double-encode the class × cohort post-materialist interaction, inflating vocationally-absorbed probability for professional × 2010s Uncs beyond empirically defensible levels

success_hints: Locate specific WVS cross-tabulation tables (Inglehart 1997, likely ch.3 or the appendix) that report post-materialism index by occupational class and cohort simultaneously. Use those numbers to derive additive class-gap estimates; convert to multipliers by dividing the class-specific post-materialism rate by the population-average rate.

For D7, check whether Inglehart reports the class gap as approximately constant across cohorts (consistent with additive-baseline-diff) or widening with later cohorts (consistent with multiplicative-on-cohort). Report the specific table that supports the proposed shape decision.

For D2-Family5 vocation-substrate couplings, if the source is primarily synthesis-2026-05-20, accept that designation but verify the multiplier magnitudes are conservative enough to avoid overclaiming — a synthesis-sourced multiplier of 1.3–1.8 is more defensible than 3.0+.
task_context: The review target is the 9 deliverables document for the Unc Rancher bias-roll matrix empirical convergence (solwend-var). This agent reviews D2-Family2 (Inglehart class × posture multiplier table), D2-Family5 (vocation-substrate couplings), and D7 (Inglehart class-interaction shape decision), checking that Inglehart's additive post-materialism finding is correctly encoded and that cells for post-1997 class categories are not mis-cited as Inglehart literature-tier.
